title: Green passes Molina late to win Lausitzring Race 1
dek: Jamie Green, without working DRS, passed pole-sitter Miguel Molina on lap 25 and won Saturday's 32-lap DTM race by 4.261 seconds, leading an Audi one-two-three-four and taking the championship lead.

chapters.title: Two races a weekend, and Audi unbeaten
text: The Lausitzring was the second of nine race weekends in a DTM season that returned to two races on each weekend: a 40-minute sprint on Saturday evening, where a tyre stop was optional, and a one-hour race on Sunday with a compulsory tyre change. Each race had its own 20-minute qualifying session, and the old option tyre had been dropped in favour of a single Hankook compound.

Audi arrived with both Hockenheim races in the bag. Jamie Green had won the opener for Team Rosberg and Mattias Ekström the second race for Abt Sportsline, which left Edoardo Mortara leading the standings on 30 points from Green and Ekström, both on 25. The Lausitzring also brought the first performance weights of the year, set from the Hockenheim results. Audi carried the most ballast, with Mortara's and Mike Rockenfeller's cars the heaviest in the field, Mercedes ran at base weight and BMW had the lightest cars. Mercedes had been Audi's closest challenger at Hockenheim, while BMW had made the weakest start of the three brands.

The DTM layout of roughly 3.5 kilometres uses a stretch of the oval, with speeds above 240 km/h before Turn 1, and the circuit was still regarded as Mercedes territory. Friday did not settle it: BMW rookie Tom Blomqvist topped the first session ahead of Ekström, and Green led the second, a pointer to a stronger Audi weekend than the ballast table suggested.

chapters.title: Molina takes pole by 0.121 seconds
text: The 20-minute session was a two-run affair, because the tyre allocation for qualifying and both races was four sets. Green set the early benchmark and traded fastest laps with Ekström, then most of the field pitted after ten minutes and the track emptied. Wehrlein was first back out and moved up to third before the final runs reshuffled everything.

Miguel Molina produced the lap of the session, a 1m17.438s for Audi Sport Team Abt Sportsline, his first pole of the 2015 season and his fourth in the DTM. Green was second, 0.121 seconds adrift, with Mortara 0.126 off and Ekström, who had also had a spin, 0.169 behind, so Audi held the whole of the front two rows. Green said afterwards that his lap had not been clean and that he was feeling unwell.

Wehrlein was the best of the rest in fifth for Mercedes, 0.183 seconds off the pole time, with Marco Wittmann sixth for BMW after his own spin, then Robert Wickens, Maxime Martin, Blomqvist and Paul di Resta. Wittmann was then given a five-place grid penalty for blocking Timo Scheider early in the session and started 11th, which lifted Scheider to tenth on the grid. Augusto Farfus, who spun on his way to 19th, started 23rd, and Adrien Tambay, who took no part in the timed running, was last of the 24. The top 22 were covered by 0.883 seconds.

chapters.title: Four Audis, one BMW and a broken splitter
text: Molina kept the lead into the first corner and the order behind him stayed Green, Mortara, Ekström. The real mover was Martin, who started seventh and was up to fifth within the opening laps, the only BMW able to stay with the Audi quartet. Farfus was less fortunate: he was pushed onto the grass early on, took contact from another car and, with a damaged front splitter, retired after two laps, the only retirement of the race.

For most of the race the four leaders were never more than two seconds apart, and Molina was at most 0.6 seconds clear of Green. Green had a problem that mattered: his DRS did not work, which made it hard to attack Molina and to keep Mortara at bay. He stayed in the leader's wake and waited. Around lap 20 Molina's advantage was down to 0.3 seconds.

chapters.title: Wehrlein moves up, Wittmann drops out of the points
text: Behind the Audis the Mercedes cars gradually worked forward. Wehrlein, who had made a poor start, got past fellow Mercedes driver Wickens for sixth and then set about Martin, whose BMW was losing grip as the stint wore on. Blomqvist, who had run as high as seventh, was passed by Wehrlein and later made a braking error at Turn 8 and ran across the gravel, finishing 22nd.

Further back, Wittmann spent much of the race with Daniel Juncadella on his bumper in the fight for tenth. Around lap 20 his tyres went away, a problem he put down to overworking them behind other cars, and Rockenfeller and then Juncadella passed him. By that point Audi had six cars in the top ten, Mercedes three and BMW only Martin, and Wittmann slid to 13th.

chapters.title: Green dives inside, Molina loses three places
text: With about eight minutes left Green finally found the gap. At the start of lap 25 he braked late and went down the inside of Molina at Turn 1, a move the pole-sitter had not expected, and built a second's lead within a lap. Mortara passed the fading Molina on lap 26 and Ekström followed on lap 27, so in three laps the leader of the first 24 had fallen to fourth. Molina's tyres were fading as the pressure built.

Green went on to win by 4.261 seconds from Mortara, with Ekström 5.220 seconds back and Molina 6.969 seconds behind, and he set the fastest lap of the race on lap 26. Wehrlein got past Martin at Turn 1 for fifth, 8.122 seconds adrift, and Wickens took sixth from the BMW on the last lap, while Martin held seventh, 13.014 seconds behind, from a late challenge by Scheider. Rockenfeller and Juncadella took ninth and tenth.

It was Green's second win of the season, and it put him top of the standings on 50 points, two clear of Mortara on 48 with Ekström on 40. Green, who was unwell and could barely speak on the radio, called the car perfect. Audi's DTM chief Dieter Gass called a one-two-three-four a rare result at a circuit that had been hard for the brand, while BMW's Jens Marquardt said his cars could not get the best from the tyres over the distance.

facts.v: Green took the lead from Molina into Turn 1 at the start of lap 25, and Mortara and Ekström both passed Molina on the following two laps.
